Record Class ActivationPolicy

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Record
com.macstab.chaos.jvm.api.ActivationPolicy
Record Components:
startMode - when the scenario begins accepting matches
probability - fraction of matches that result in effect application; in (0.0, 1.0]
activateAfterMatches - number of initial matches to skip before the effect becomes eligible
maxApplications - hard cap on total effect applications; null means unlimited
activeFor - time window during which the scenario remains active; null means none
rateLimit - fixed-window rate cap on applications; null means unlimited
randomSeed - fixed PRNG seed for reproducible probability sampling; null draws a random seed from ThreadLocalRandom on first activation — sampling is non-deterministic across JVM restarts; set an explicit value for reproducible sequences
allowDestructiveEffects - whether destructive effects (deadlocks, thread leaks) may be activated
activeFrom - wall-clock instant before which the scenario does not fire; null means no lower bound. Read from the real system clock, so a clock skew the agent injects cannot move it
activeUntil - wall-clock instant from which on the scenario no longer fires and becomes INACTIVE; null means no upper bound. Read from the real system clock
replayMatches - the 1-based match numbers on which the scenario fires, in place of the probability draw: a decision log recorded by ChaosDecisionRecorder replayed exactly. null means no replay. Sorted, distinct and positive; requires probability 1.0 and no rate limit, which would change the decisions
public record ActivationPolicy(ActivationPolicy.StartMode startMode, double probability, long activateAfterMatches, @Nullable Long maxApplications, @Nullable Duration activeFor, @Nullable ActivationPolicy.RateLimit rateLimit, @Nullable Long randomSeed, boolean allowDestructiveEffects, @Nullable Instant activeFrom, @Nullable Instant activeUntil, @Nullable List<Long> replayMatches) extends Record
Controls when and how often a chaos effect fires when its selector matches an operation.

All constraints are conjunctive: a match must satisfy every active constraint before the effect is applied. A null constraint means "no restriction on this axis".

Quick references:

  • always() — effect fires on every match, starts immediately
  • manual() — effect fires on every match, but only after ChaosActivationHandle.start() is called
  • withDestructiveEffects() — same as always() but with explicit opt-in for destructive effects (deadlock(), threadLeak())

Fine-grained control via the builder (prefer it to the positional constructors, whose argument order is easy to misplace): 

// Fire with 30% probability, cap at 100 total applications, seeded for reproducibility.
ActivationPolicy.builder()
    .probability(0.30)
    .maxApplications(100L)
    .randomSeed(42L)
    .build();

Destructive effects: ChaosEffect.DeadlockEffect and ChaosEffect.ThreadLeakEffect hold deadlocked or parked threads, with their locks and memory, until the scenario is stopped (stopping or closing it interrupts and ends them); leaked non-daemon threads also keep the JVM from exiting until then. Activation of these effects requires allowDestructiveEffects(true) in the policy; any attempt without it throws ChaosValidationException at registration time, not at effect application time. Use them in test processes or controlled environments.

  • Constructor Details

    • ActivationPolicy

      public ActivationPolicy(ActivationPolicy.StartMode startMode, double probability, long activateAfterMatches, @Nullable Long maxApplications, @Nullable Duration activeFor, @Nullable ActivationPolicy.RateLimit rateLimit, @Nullable Long randomSeed, boolean allowDestructiveEffects, @Nullable Instant activeFrom, @Nullable Instant activeUntil, @Nullable List<Long> replayMatches)
      Compact canonical constructor — normalises defaults and validates all field invariants.

      A null startMode defaults to ActivationPolicy.StartMode.AUTOMATIC. An explicit probability of 0.0 is rejected: a user writing probability: 0.0 in a config file is almost certainly trying to disable the effect, and silently rewriting it to 1.0 turns an "off" switch into an "always fire" switch. The error message redirects to omitting the scenario activation entirely, which actually expresses "never fire".

      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if probability is outside (0.0, 1.0], or if activateAfterMatches is negative, or if maxApplications or activeFor violate their constraints

  • Method Details

    • always

      public static ActivationPolicy always()
      Returns a policy that fires on every match and starts immediately on activation.

      Equivalent to: probability=1.0, startMode=AUTOMATIC, no other constraints. Uses the fixed seed 0, so sampled delays of a delay range are reproducible across runs; pass randomSeed = null to the constructor for a random seed. A scenario without a policy gets this one, so in plan JSON a scenario without activationPolicy has seed 0, while an activationPolicy that omits randomSeed (or sets it to null) draws a random one.

      Returns:
      an always-fire activation policy

    • withDestructiveEffects

      public static ActivationPolicy withDestructiveEffects()
      Returns a policy that fires on every match, starts immediately, and explicitly permits destructive effects (ChaosEffect.DeadlockEffect, ChaosEffect.ThreadLeakEffect).

      Warning: a destructive effect holds deadlocked or leaked threads, with their locks and memory, until the scenario is stopped or closed; leaked non-daemon threads also keep the JVM from exiting until then. Use it in test processes.

      Returns:
      an always-fire activation policy that permits destructive effects

    • manual

      public static ActivationPolicy manual()
      Returns a policy that fires on every match but starts in the REGISTERED state. The effect does not fire until ChaosActivationHandle.start() is called. Uses the fixed seed 0, like always().

      Use for synchronised test phases where chaos must be enabled at a precise moment.

      Returns:
      an activation policy that fires on every match but starts in REGISTERED state

    • count

      public static ActivationPolicy count(long applications)
      Returns a policy that fires on the first applications matches and then becomes INACTIVE: always() with maxApplications = applications. The equivalent of the native library's @first=N qualifier.
      Parameters:
      applications - the number of applications; > 0
      Returns:
      the policy
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if applications is not positive

    • window

      public static ActivationPolicy window(@Nullable Instant from, @Nullable Instant until)
      Returns a policy that fires on every match between two wall-clock instants: always() with activeFrom = from and activeUntil = until. The equivalent of the native library's @from/@until qualifiers. Either bound may be null.
      Parameters:
      from - the first instant the scenario fires at; null for no lower bound
      until - the instant from which on the scenario no longer fires; null for no upper bound
      Returns:
      the policy
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if from is not before until

    • builder

      public static ActivationPolicy.Builder builder()
      Returns a builder whose defaults equal always(): automatic start, probability 1.0, no warm-up, cap, window or rate limit, seed 0, no destructive effects.
      Returns:
      a new builder
